No actions this turn. Before writing it up, I need you to pick how it gets built, in one quick message.

Understood, I'll write it up next. First, one decision we haven't covered: how it gets built. It changes the whole design, so here are the two real options, both running on the Pi you already have:

**A. Add it to the taproom app.** You'd get new batch, sack and bottling screens and new tables in the same SQLite database. The scanner works as a USB "keyboard" into a browser page. You'd have one thing to run and back up, and it's the least work. The trade-off is that your trace records live alongside the tab code. A bad update to tabs could take batch tracking down with it, or the other way round.

**B. A separate small app on the same Pi, with its own database file.** It would use the same tools (Flask, SQLite, browser and scanner), but the two apps stay separate. It's slightly more setup: a second service and a second file to back up. The benefit is that your recall records never depend on taproom changes, and each part stays small and easy to reason about.

I'd skip off-the-shelf brewery software. What you've described depends on scanning your own sack lots and your own label printer, which those tools generally don't fit well.

**My recommendation is B.** If you ever need to trace a bottle for a recall, that record should be the most dependable thing you own, and it shouldn't be at risk from a change to how tabs work.

Once you pick, I'll write the full design. A reviewer will read it before I hand it over, and I may come back once with a few quick questions.

Which way do you want to go, A or B?
